item.title: NASA spots a giant patch of Moon-like rock on Earth
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: ScienceDaily.
Summary: An astronaut aboard the International Space Station photographed a remarkable formation in Madagascar that looks surprisingly similar to the Moon’s bright highlands. Made of anorthosite, a rock abundant on the lunar surface, the formation dates back at least 600 million years and bears the scars of ancient continental collisions.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside in the Northern New Jersey, the useful question is observational: check whether the event is visible from your latitude and how moonlight interferes. item.title: How a cold pulse in the Northwest Atlantic reshaped East Coast fisheries
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: Fishers in the Northeast began noticing an unusual shift in the summer of 2023. Some familiar catches, including shortfin and longfin squid, declined, while cold-water species such as mackerel bounced back from years of decline. A new study published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans finds that a pulse of cold, fresh water brought unusually cold conditions to the region, disrupting fisheries from New England to the Mid-Atlantic.
Waypoint’s Take: Outside in the Northeast, this matters because it can change what you watch for: read rock exposure, erosion, and landform clues as part of the landscape story.
